author: hoeschec
text:
I am wondering if many of my engulf trades fail because I am not engulfing the source of the move (engulfing important structure). Now that I am practicing S/R flips, I wonder if the source of the move (that also contains the DP) is the FL that needs to be EG in order for a setup or QM to be valid.

Here is an example on E/U. It's just a 1-min chart, but it is a good example of what would trick me. At first glance (to me) it looks like a QM setup. But the source of the move that broke the S/R has not been engulfed, so it is not valid.

But then there is the complication of scale. Same chart, but on a 5 min time frame (a few mins have passed since I took the screen shot of the 1 min chart, so price has progressed a bit). On the 5 min chart, it looks like an engulf would require price to break out of a larger FL. Very subjective, very frustrating. I'd say when in doubt go with the higher time frame.

I'll keep practicing these to see if I am on the right track.

And then there is the further complication (once you determine which FL needs to be broken to signal the engulf) of judging whether the price break is really an engulf or just a fakeout. My understanding is it depends on where price breaks to. Price that breaks in to an important zone containing orders (FL, FTR, S/R Flip etc...) is likely a F/O. So in the case below (EUR-USD) price has finally broken the 5 min source, however it is clear price also tagged a S/R zone creating an S/R flip. So do we have an engulf or a F/O? And how would we judge this in real time without waiting for PA to form and make it obvious in hindsight?

I have marked the S/R where price broke through the FL and touched.

author: hoeschec
text:
Josh- I noticed your stop loss is pretty tight. Did you zoom in to find the DP and place a stop just above that point? I'd love to have the confidence to place a tight stop like that, but I don't want to get stopped out if price retraces back to the upper limit of the supply zone before dropping.

I love these setups, but I have a hard time actually executing a trade. Stop placement has always been an issue for me (ex: how do you handle a diamond formation?). I guess it depends on how much risk one is willing to take.

Technically, price could turn at the QM level (previous high), but if I take a position there, the stop is going to be wide. If I place my entry close to the origin of the engulf or the decision point, the stop will be smaller.

I have an irrational fear of missing out on really nice setups like U/J which usually makes me execute too early.

I posted a chart below that illustrates what I am describing.
